tasks.short: Turn yearly pay and benefits analysis into a reward report, a benefits guide on SharePoint and a works council briefing.

today.trigger: Yearly cycle: after the CAO wage round and the annual salary review, or when the works council or HR Director asks for the pay and benefits overview.
steps: Pull salary, allowance and benefit data from the AFAS extract and Power BI into Excel
Write up findings (pay band position, CAO scale adherence, gender pay gap, benefit uptake) in Word
Update the employee benefits guide and policy pages on SharePoint
Build a PowerPoint for the HR Director and the works council
Rework text and charts after review rounds
drudgery: Rebuilding the same charts and tables every year
Rewriting the same findings for three audiences (management, works council, employees)
Checking that figures in the text match the spreadsheet after each revision
today.time_sinks: Formatting and keeping numbers consistent across report, slides and guide, and rewriting for each audience after review comments.

lenses.faster: A fixed Power BI and Excel template feeds the numbers; an LLM drafts the narrative and the audience versions, so the specialist edits instead of writing from scratch.
lenses.autonomous: After the nightly AFAS extract following the salary review is locked, the tables, charts and a first draft are generated without anyone asking.
lenses.ambitious: Publish a proper yearly reward statement per employee and a pay equity report ready for the EU Pay Transparency Directive, instead of one internal deck.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses reformatting charts and chasing mismatched numbers; what remains is interpreting the findings and deciding what to say to the works council.
lenses.options: Draft the same findings in three to five forms: a management memo, a works council briefing, a plain-language employee page in Dutch and English, and a short explainer video script.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the report template, the data definitions and the review checklist, and checks the generated output rather than producing it.
reach: Pay gap and pay equity reporting now done ad hoc by the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst
Benefits pages and FAQs on SharePoint maintained by HR Administrators
Personnel cost commentary for the FP&A Analyst's budget pack

tasks.human_edge: Choosing what to disclose and how to frame pay gaps and CAO deviations for the works council and employees; that carries trust and legal weight.
tasks.pattern_why: A once-a-year, judgment-heavy write-up for sensitive audiences; AI drafts text and versions from fixed numbers, the specialist leads and signs off.

in_practice.trigger: Salary review data locked in AFAS and the nightly Power BI refresh completed.
steps: Power BI report template refreshes pay, gap and benefit uptake tables
LLM drafts the narrative and audience versions from the tables and last year's report
Automated check compares every number in the text with the source tables
Specialist edits framing, removes sensitive detail, gets HR Director approval
Publish to SharePoint and send the works council briefing
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist and HR Director approve every version before it goes to the works council or employees.
systems: Microsoft 365 Copilot or an approved LLM
data_needed: Aggregated salary and allowance data by CAO scale, function and gender
Last year's report and CAO texts
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint document library with version history and approval record

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot drafts Word documents and PowerPoint decks from files and data in the tenant.
Power BI can generate narrative summaries of report visuals.
evidence.source: Power BI smart narrative / Copilot in Power BI

evidence.claim: Drafting audience-specific versions of a pay report cuts writing time roughly in half.

risks: Small groups in pay gap tables can identify individuals (AVG/GDPR)
LLM text states a number or trend that is not in the data
Wording on pay gaps or CAO deviations creates expectations or disputes with the works council
Salary data sent to a model outside the approved Microsoft tenant
research_questions: How many hours did last year's reward report and works council briefing actually take, and how much was rewriting?
Is Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed and approved for HR data at Noordhaven, and under which data processing terms?
What does the Dutch implementation of the EU Pay Transparency Directive require Noordhaven to publish, and from when?
Does the works council want a recurring pay report, and in what form?

role.altitude: From producing pay analyses and documents to owning the reward data model, report templates and rules (CAO scales, allowances, benefits) that generate them, and checking their output.
reach: Pay transparency and gender pay gap reporting with the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst
Payroll input checks on allowances and CAO increases with the Payroll Specialist
Personnel cost forecasting with the FP&A Analyst
Benefits questions and SharePoint content now handled by HR Administrators
role.ceiling_note: This task is about 16 hours a year, so the saving here is small; the larger gains sit in recurring work like salary reviews, CAO increases and benchmarking. Limits are judgment on pay decisions, works council consultation, AVG/GDPR on salary data, and AI Act care if models influence individual pay.
skills_to_grow: Power BI and data modelling on the AFAS extract
Writing and checking LLM prompts and templates
Pay equity analysis and EU Pay Transparency Directive requirements
Explaining reward choices to the works council in plain language
role.ambitious_version: Run a pay transparency function: per-employee reward statements, a yearly pay equity report and live salary band checks on every offer and promotion, all generated from AFAS and reviewed by one specialist.
